results.title: Ramayana actor Ravie Dubey once struggled to afford food. How he went from earning Rs 10,000 per month to building a Rs 80 crore fortune
results.description: Ramayana actor Ravie Dubey's journey took a tumultuous turn when he relocated to Mumbai to pursue engineering after 2001. Battling academic setbacks and the weight of societal expectations led him into a dark phase of mental health struggles. However, a serendipitous audition while studying shifted his trajectory, leading to his first paycheck in 2005. His breakout role came with the series Saas Bina Sasural in 2010, followed by Jamai Raja in 2014.

results.title: Virat Kohli Turns 38: 'King Kohli' Receives Heartwarming Birthday Wishes As Cricket Fraternity And Fans Flood Social Media With Love
results.description: Virat Kohli celebrates his 38th birthday on November 5, with wishes pouring in from fans, former cricketers, celebrities & the cricket fraternity. Social media is flooded with heartfelt messages celebrating the Indian batting star's incredible career and achievements. The former India captain's birthday has turned into a global celebration, with fans showering their beloved 'King Kohli' with love.

results.title: Florida Governor calls Midterm rout 'close to extinction-level event', says Republicans failed to 'shut off H-1B visas'
results.description: Washington, Nov 5 (IANS) Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has faulted Senate Republicans for failing to curb the H-1B visa programme, the main route by which Indian technology professionals work in the United States, as he blamed the party's midterm losses partly on its own voters staying home. Asked by Fox News host Laura Ingraham how big a mistake it was not to get rid of the Senate filibuster, DeSantis said he "saw no indication that the current group of Republican senators were interested in doing that type of conservative change." "I mean, why haven't we done immigration, shut off H-1B visas? Why haven't we codified Trump's immigration executive orders?" he told Ingraham. He also asked why Republicans had not "stripped jurisdiction from the federal courts over deportation cases." "There's so many things that could have been done, they didn't even attempt it," DeSantis said. Custom Ad: Multiplex He said the midterm result was "a rebuke of the president and the Congress by Democrats, independents and some Republicans that crossed over." But, he added, "a lot of our voters who stayed home, they stayed home because they were frustrated with the lack of productivity from Republicans in the House and Senate." "So it's really both sides of Pennsylvania Avenue. It's not just one," he said. At a news conference in Florida on Wednesday, DeSantis called Tuesday's results "close to an extinction-level event for Republicans in many parts of the country, as we have seen probably in the last 100 years." "This was not a positive view of the Democrats. This was a rejection of Republicans in Washington and Democrats just happened to be the beneficiary," he said. He said Republicans in Texas, long "the crown jewel of Republican politics", had lost "a very highly publicised US Senate race" and "the governor, attorney general, all the other statewide" offices. "If the Republican Party doesn't have Texas as an anchor, then we're not gonna be viable nationally going forward," he said. Republicans lost control of both the House and the Senate on Tuesday, while Republican Byron Donalds won the race to succeed DeSantis, Fox News reported. DeSantis, who leaves office in January and has not ruled out a 2028 presidential run, has made H-1B a recurring target. At an event near Lakeland on September 14, he said: "I think we should eliminate H-1B visas in the United States, to be quite frank," Fox 49 reported. Indians are by far the largest beneficiaries of the programme. According to the latest annual report to Congress by US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), released in April, 70 per cent of the roughly 406,000 H-1B petitions approved in fiscal 2025 were for beneficiaries born in India. China was a distant second at about 12 per cent. Indians made up about 78 per cent of approvals for continuing employment. The programme allows US employers to hire foreign workers in speciality occupations, largely in technology. It is capped at 65,000 new visas a year, plus 20,000 for holders of US advanced degrees. Ending it would require legislation from Congress, which Democrats will control from January. --IANS lkj/sd/

results.title: Bengal’s new industrial policy to be announced today, focus on ‘ease of doing business’
results.description: Kolkata, Nov 5 (IANS) West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari will announce the state government's new industrial policy on Thursday, with a focus on 'ease of doing business' by removing unnecessary government regulations for investment proposals and ensuring quick approvals. At the same time, state secretariat insiders aware of the contents of the new industrial policy said there will be proposals to resurrect the state’s incentive policy for investors, which was done away with during the previous Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress regime, in a more structured and comprehensive manner. “The draft industrial policy had been designed as per the policies adopted by industrially developed states,” a state secretariat insider said. The state cabinet cleared the draft industrial policy on October 28. Now the final industrial policy will be announced on Thursday afternoon after an administrative review meeting at the state Secretariat 'Nabanna'. Custom Ad: Multiplex The new industrial policy has been drafted by a group of ministers, and industrialists, industry associations, and economic experts were also consulted. “Since the state government wanted the new industrial policy to be more structured and comprehensive, making a balance between various factors like investors’ interest, employment generation possibilities and the interest of the other stakeholders like landowners whose land will be acquired for industrial projects, the deadline for announcing the same was postponed again and again,” said sources in the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC). Initially, it was announced that the new industrial policy would be announced on August 15 on the occasion of Independence Day. However, that did not happen, and the deadline was postponed repeatedly. Finally, on October 28, the draft industrial policy received the state cabinet nod, and it was announced that the policy would be formally announced on Thursday. As regards the proposed incentives to be announced for investors in the new industrial policy, state secretariat insiders said the focus would be on attracting investment to backward areas so that industrial projects developed there can be linked to socio-economic development in the area. "The incentives can be in the form of waiver of electricity tariff for the initial years of project implementation and operations, state government bearing a certain percentage of interest on loans taken by the entrepreneur concerned, and reimbursement of the company’s contribution in employees' provident fund, among others," a state government official said. After taking charge as the ninth Chief Minister of West Bengal in May this year, Suvendu Adhikari announced that a comprehensive new industrial policy will be formulated and announced within the current year to facilitate big-ticket investment in the state. Accordingly, a group of ministers was entrusted with the task of drawing up the new policy in June, Before the announcement of the new industrial policy, the Chief Minister had claimed that the policy had been prepared with a focus on creating an ideal investment ambience in the state, removing red-tapism in approvals, and ensuring massive employment generation. --IANS src/dpb
